messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: intel compiler and Stan...
parts:
Hi!

... be warned: You have to use the right compiler options; otherwise you will not see divergences!

I am using the Intel compiler 15.0.3 and I just ran a model for which I know that divergences do happen, but I did not get any. I went back and noticed that my model was compiled with the defaults which is to use optimization as per default from Intel. This leads to failures of the stan-math unit tests AND it seems to be the root cause for stopping Stan to report divergences. So to get the behavior which makes stan-math unit tests succeed you must use the options

-fp-model precise -fp-model source

Note that the Intel compiler is not an "official" compiler, but be warned when using it. This means you need to include this into your ~/.R/Makevars file in the definition of the CXXFLAGS, respectivley for cmdstan.

Best,
Sebastian
